title: DG ISPR Holds Marka-e-Haq Anniversary Presser; Confirms Op Ghazab lil-Haq Ongoing, Rejects Civilian Casualty Allegations
detail:
May 7, 2026 (Day 71 of Operation Ghazab lil-Haq): Pakistan's Director General Inter-Services Public Relations, Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, held a high-profile press conference marking the first anniversary of Operation Marka-e-Haq — Pakistan's May 2025 military confrontation with India. Chaudhry was flanked by Rear Admiral Shifaat Ali Khan and Air Vice Marshal Tariq Mahmood Ghazi, signalling a joint-service deliberate messaging event.

On the Afghanistan front, Chaudhry explicitly confirmed Operation Ghazab lil-Haq remains ongoing, stating: 'Ghazab lil-Haq's linkage is with the actions of the Afghan Taliban regime.' Pakistan's military categorically rejected the Afghan Taliban's civilian casualty allegations from the May 5 Dangam, Kunar strikes, reaffirming that all strikes remain 'focused, precise, and directed solely against infiltrators, terrorist hideouts, and support infrastructures.'

Chaudhry also introduced a new framing linking the Af-Pak operation to the India-Pakistan strategic rivalry, claiming TTP and other militant groups attacking Pakistani soil are operationally enabled by 'India-sponsored terror' networks using Afghan territory as a base. This narrative — connecting Pakistan's anti-India posture with its anti-TTP campaign in Afghanistan — represents a significant escalation in Pakistan's diplomatic framing, apparently intended to marshal domestic support for the ongoing operation and pre-empt international criticism of civilian casualties.

The joint-service presence and anniversary timing indicated a deliberate military signalling effort: Pakistan intends to maintain its operational tempo in Afghanistan as part of a broader national security posture, not merely a reactive counterterrorism campaign.

media.caption: Pakistan DG ISPR Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry confirms Operation Ghazab lil-Haq remains ongoing at Marka-e-Haq anniversary press conference, May 7, 2026

title: Pakistan Signals Willingness to Extend Operational Pause in Op Ghazab Conditionally — No New Strikes If Afghan Territory Kept Clear of TTP
detail:
May 7, 2026: Pakistani media outlet Abb Takk reported that Pakistan is signalling a willingness to extend its operational pause within Operation Ghazab lil-Haq on a conditional basis — specifically, that no new cross-border strikes would be launched as long as no attacks against Pakistani territory originate from Afghan soil and TTP (Fitna al-Khawarij) is not allowed to regroup in Afghan border areas.

The signal is a conditional de-escalation posture, distinct from a formal ceasefire. Pakistan has not publicly declared a pause and DG ISPR's May 7 presser simultaneously confirmed the operation remains active. The conditional framing mirrors Pakistan's overall diplomatic position: operations will continue until the Taliban provides 'credible guarantees' on TTP, but tactical pauses may occur if Afghan behavior warrants them.

The development is significant in the context of mounting international pressure: UK Special Envoy Lindsay's May 1 criticism, the UN's May 3 alarm over Afghan deportations, and the Taliban's diplomatic escalation following the May 5 Dangam civilian casualty incident. Pakistan appears to be creating diplomatic space for itself — presenting as open to de-escalation — while maintaining the military option and linking any ceasefire to Taliban action on TTP.

No formal ceasefire proposal has been made, no new Urumqi Round 2 date has been set, and China has not publicly commented on the latest developments. The Afghan Taliban has not responded to Pakistan's conditional framing as of May 7.

media.caption: Pakistan signals conditional willingness to extend operational pause in Op Ghazab lil-Haq if Afghan territory is not used for TTP attacks — Abb Takk, May 7, 2026
